rules.coverage_after_migration: An evidence gap is FATAL unless the task's remaining required commands INDEPENDENTLY cover the claim. The migration must SAY SO per task, naming the commands that cover it; the validator then enforces the verdict, and the covering commands are themselves validated strictly. A verdict of SUPPORTED with no named covering command is refused.
rules.evidence_absent: a legacy entry whose evidence was never retained is recorded here and MUST NOT be relied upon as closure evidence; the task's other commands must stand on their own
rules.log_free_preflights: a toolchain probe (a version command) produceth no evidence of behavior and needeth no log; it existeth to record the executor, and it is declared here rather than exempted by a blanket rule
rules.mutation_records: a mutation record is a MUTATION LINEAGE record and is VALIDATED AS ONE by the checker (AUDIT-004): it must name the source identity, retain a real log whose sha256 match, name the killed cases in a failure roster that is RE-READ from that log, and name its restored-green rerun. The label alone, an arbitrary note, a nonzero exit or a compile failure is NOT a semantic kill. A mutation record whose evidence was NEVER RETAINED is an EVIDENCE GAP and is listed under evidence_absent_do_not_rely -- it is never an EXEMPTION and may never be counted as a behavioral test pass

outcome_vocabulary.MUTANT_KILLED: a MUTATION record, never a test pass

rules.required_commands: a COMPLETE task's required list must name commands that PASSED with exit 0 and carry a retained log; a command that FAILED and hath a later PASSING attempt of the same stage is SUBSTITUTED, and the failure is preserved as history

T05.coverage_note: T05's behavioral evidence is its narrow and subsystem gradle logs (retained). The two XML audits were SUMMARIES written without a retained roster, so they are recorded as evidence_absent and are NOT relied upon. AUDIT-004 (step 5) removed the former `mutation_records` entry: that record's own evidence -- a log, a failure roster, a source identity and a restored-green rerun -- was NEVER RETAINED, so under the enforced law it cannot be validated as a mutation lineage record and is now recorded as the evidence gap it always was. The mutation control is therefore NOT ESTABLISHED by it, and nothing here claimeth that it is.

T05-mutation-commit-before-aead.why: the mutant-killed lineage record carrieth NO retained log (log_path and log_sha256 are both null), NO failure roster field (the two killed case names live only in free-text `note`), NO source_sha/tree_sha identity and NO restored-green companion command. Under the law the checker now enforces (AUDIT-004 step 3) such a record can never be validated as a mutation lineage record. The MUTATION CONTROL IT ASSERTED IS THEREFORE NOT ESTABLISHED, and this migration doth not assert that it is: it is recorded as a gap, not exempted. T05's own behavioral claim -- that the replay-window / AEAD ordering holds -- is carried independently by the retained narrow and subsystem gradle logs and the control checks, none of which rest on this record.

why: The audit reproduced that the completion validator accepted failed commands, missing logs and evidence-free COMPLETE entries. Making the validator strict exposes the historical records that were written under the OLD, looser conventions. This file is the EXPLICIT migration the card requireth: every reinterpretation of a legacy entry is named, reasoned and refutable, and NOTHING is deleted -- the failed attempts stay in their manifests as history.
